title: Self-knowledge
text: Studying ethics in higher education is as much about self-discovery and self-scrutiny as it is about learning ethical theories or the writings of philosophers. The activities commonly involve sorting and trading value cards, prompting students to reflect on their most deeply held convictions and justify those to others but mainly to themselves. Through these activities, students gain a better understanding of themselves and develop a nuanced understanding of what really matters to them.

title: Engagement across differences
text: In line with our center's focus on civil discourse, the Value Cards and their activities are designed to help facilitate conversations across disagreements. Reflecting on values together, especially in activities that require trade-offs (like trading), reveals our different perspectives in a way that sheds light on disagreements concerning specific policies or outcomes. Discussion of values often helps see others' view in a more favorable light, or see that despite disagreement on specifics there is still agreement on shared values.

title: Experience a deliberative process
text: Experience a deliberation process with conflicting interests and distributed knowledge, in the context of a formal and structured process enacting collective/public decisions.

title: Practice civil discourse skills
text: Practice civil discourse skills, namely engaging in productive conversations across differences in the context of matters of mutual concern when the stakes are sufficiently high.

title: Face trade-offs between moral values and strategic goals
text: Face trade-offs between moral values and strategic goals, and take a stand by making decisions in the exercise, which is real enough to reveal positions but still low-stakes enough to treat those as a learning experience.
